events.what: Brendle and Hung preprint claims a metric of positive sectional curvature on S^2 x S^2, refuting the product form of the Hopf conjecture
events.credibility_reason: Established authors and a serious method, but an automated verifier (Refine) reported a Mathematica bug in the second-order positivity reduction and a gap in a uniform bound; the v2 changelog mentions only typographical fixes. Automated review is not a knock-down (F11), and no human expert has confirmed the error.

events.what: Kennard-Mouillé-Nienhaus (arXiv:2507.16936) and arXiv:2507.15237 on restricted/variant settings of the sign form

judgement.doubts: The bullet names 'the Hopf conjectures' (plural); refuting the product form leaves the sign form open, so this is a case (F2). Correctness is genuinely in doubt pending human reading of the Refine-flagged points; the full Golub thread was not read (HTTP 402), only snippets. The 2507.15237 locally-conformally-flat result might be argued a case rather than a variant, but it would not change the tier. No searches run.

corrections.why: F1/F2: the record's own summary says the construction 'refutes the product form outright ... while leaving the sign form untouched'; the bullet names both Hopf conjectures, so this is a case, i.e. partial regardless of review state.

F9/F11: Refine only criticised the human preprint ('flaws that @RefineDotInk says need to be resolved'); an AI critic produced none of the mathematics in the result, and the authors' Mathematica use is computer algebra, not AI. The basis quote is kept as evidence of the dispute.

other: kept, but the refutation rests on an unreviewed preprint with unanswered Refine-flagged gaps; if a human confirms the Mathematica bug is fatal the event becomes knocked_down and the status open.
